citations.F1: Kill the N+1: `serialize_event` awaits one `users` fetch per event, sequentially, so limit=1000 means 1,000 extra round trips — join `users` in the main query, or batch with `WHERE id = ANY($1)`.
citations.F2: Replace the `seen` list with a set — `ev["dedupe_key"] in seen` is O(n²) over the full window
citations.F3: `lookup_geo` uses blocking `requests.get` (2 s timeout) inside an async handler, so each uncached IP stalls the whole worker's event loop and `/healthz` with it — switch to an async client, or `run_in_executor`
citations.F4: Add `CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY events_org_created_idx ON events (org_id, created_at DESC)` — the only indexes are on `actor_id` and `kind`, so the query seq-scans 4.2M rows
citations.F5: `_request_timings` grows one float per request forever ... replace with a fixed-size `deque` or a bucketed histogram
citations.F6: Bound `_geo_cache` too — unbounded dict keyed on client IP, never evicted, a slower second leak; use an LRU with a TTL.
citations.F9: do not ship it; 16 workers × pool 50 × 6 pods = up to 4,800 Postgres connections ... and a 60 s Redis cache still leaves every miss blocking the event loop that kills `/healthz`
